from.place: Affine Koszul zero-detector proof, construction and open-restriction comparison

title: Affine supported Koszul object and open-unit comparison
statement: Let X be an affine scheme with chosen derived categories for module sheaves and every open restriction [def-pc-derived-category]. Let T be closed with quasi-compact complement, and let U be the open whose underlying set is X minus T. There exist a quasi-coherent derived object E, a right adjoint R to exact derived restriction to U, and an adjunction, such that E is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], every cohomology stalk of E outside T is zero, and for every quasi-coherent derived K (without any support condition), vanishing of Hom(E[n],K) for all integers n makes the canonical adjunction unit at K invertible.

proof.text: Take A to be the global section ring of X and a the inverse of X.isoSpec. The inverse image of U is compact by its homeomorphism. Mathlib eq_finite_iUnion_of_isTopologicalBasis_of_isCompact_open applied to the principal-open basis gives a finite set s of functions. Reindex s by Fin(card s) and prove that a point lies outside the inverse image of U exactly when it contains all tuple entries. No extra hypothesis excludes the empty tuple or the zero ring.

Apply the general isomorphism transport theorem to a and U. Write Q as the actual sheafified Koszul complex for the finite tuple. Its perfection and stalk support are supplied by the geometric-properties theorem. Prove quasi-coherence of Q directly: its terms are associated sheaves; homology is a cokernel of the incoming map to the outgoing kernel. Quasi-coherent sheaves are closed under kernels and cokernels, and homologyFunctorFactors identifies complex homology with derived homology. Form E as F(Q) in the quasi-coherent full subcategory. Transfer perfection and stalk support to X.

For each quasi-coherent K on X, compose Iso.homCongr for the functor shift isomorphism with F.toAdjunction.homEquiv, and use Equiv.subsingleton_congr to send its orthogonality to E to orthogonality of F^{-1}(K) to this exact Q. Apply koszul_open_orthogonality on Spec A using a, the finite tuple, the proved zero-locus equality, and the transported adjunction. Its unit is invertible. The unit comparison supplied by transport then proves invertibility of the unit on X. This explicitly uses the existing detector theorem and never infers detection from support alone.

mathlib_searches.results: No existing exact statement. Restriction vanishing is proved using TopCat.Presheaf.section_ext, ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso, DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors, and DerivedCategory.isIso_iff. KoszulOpenOrthogonality is the existing comparison input, not its transport and construction on an arbitrary affine scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem supported_perfect_detector_affine_construction
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : (U : Set X) = Tᶜ) :
    ∃ (E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X)
      (R : DerivedCategory
        (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ⥤
        schemeDerivedCategory X)
      (adj : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
        (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory ⊣ R),
      Scheme.IsPerfect X E.obj ∧
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ T →
        Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj E.obj).val.presheaf x))) ∧
      ∀ K : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X,
        (∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (E.obj⟦n⟧ ⟶ K.obj)) → IsIso (adj.unit.app K.obj)
